## Introduction

Liang Qichao 梁啟超 was one of the most widely read writers of the late Qing. His essay
〈少年中國說〉 ("On Young China", 1900) opens by answering a foreign description of China.

## Text

日本人之稱我中國也，一則曰老大帝國，再則曰老大帝國。

## Glosses

| Term | Pinyin | Gloss | Grammar |
|---|---|---|---|
| 日本人 | Rìběnrén | the Japanese | |
| 之 | zhī | *part.* placed between subject and verb, turns the clause into a noun phrase | zhi-nominaliser |
| 稱 | chēng | to call; to refer to as | |
| 我 | wǒ | I, we; here "our" | |
| 中國 | Zhōngguó | China | |
| 也 | yě | *part.* marks a pause after the topic | ye-topic |
| 一則 | yīzé | in the first place; firstly | |
| 再則 | zàizé | in the second place; and again | |
| 曰 | yuē | to say; to call (something) | |
| 老大 | lǎodà | old, aged; decrepit | |
| 帝國 | dìguó | empire | |

## Translation

When the Japanese speak of our China, they call it "the old empire", and again "the old empire".

## Literal translation

Japanese-people's calling our China — firstly say "old empire", secondly say "old empire".

## Notes

The sentence is built as **topic + comment**. The topic, 日本人之稱我中國也, is a whole
clause turned into a noun phrase by [之](../../grammar/zhi-nominaliser.md) and closed
by [也](../../grammar/ye-topic.md). The comment repeats 老大帝國 in the frame
一則曰…再則曰…, which stresses how often the label is used.

## Exercises

### 1. choice

In 日本人**之**稱我中國也, what does 之 do?

- [ ] It marks possession: "the Japanese people's China"
- [x] It makes 日本人稱我中國 into a noun phrase: "the Japanese calling our China"
- [ ] It is an object pronoun: "it"

**Explanation:** Placed between a subject (日本人) and its verb (稱), 之 turns the clause into a noun phrase, which here becomes the topic of the sentence.

### 2. punctuate

Punctuate the sentence.

**Text:** 日本人之稱我中國也一則曰老大帝國再則曰老大帝國

**Answer:** 日本人之稱我中國也，一則曰老大帝國，再則曰老大帝國。

### 3. translate

Translate the sentence into English.

**Answer:** When the Japanese speak of our China, they call it "the old empire", and again "the old empire".

**Explanation:** 曰 here means "to call (it)", not "to say". The repetition is deliberate.
